text:
Anya: Quick check-in — I prototyped splitting the allocator API into two strata: a tiny fast-path for latency-sensitive allocations and a richer policy surface for eviction/prefetch hints. Thoughts?
Kevin: Definitely interesting. Main worry is ABI churn and callers having to migrate.
Marta: Can we keep a single public API that routes to fast+policy underneath so callers don't break? Opt-in for callers that care about hints.
Anya: Yeah that's the plan — keep the old API as a compatibility shim. New surfaces: `alloc_fast(size, flags)` (lock-free, minimal metadata) and `alloc_policy(ptr, hint)` (descriptive, async-friendly).
Devon: Fast path must avoid any syscalls or heavyweight bookkeeping. Prefer per-thread freelists + atomic bump.
Kevin: Also need to define failure semantics: if fast alloc can't get a resident GPU page, do we block, return a staging handle, or fail? Each has big infra implications.
Marta: For UX, returning a lightweight staging handle that the runtime can swap in lazily seems best — caller stays non-blocking. But we need clear semantics for when that handle is upgraded to resident memory.
Anya: Proposed rule: fast alloc never blocks. It returns either resident ptr or a staging token. Runtime async-migrator upgrades tokens based on priority and SLO. Policy API can pin/annotate to force residency.
Anya: prototype snippet:```c
// fast path
void* alloc_fast(size_t sz, uint32_t flags, uint64_t* token_out);
// policy hinting
void annot_hint(uint64_t token, enum hotness);
```
Kevin: Good. Pointers: need a stable token format so we can refer to allocations after compaction/evict moves. Token -> metadata mapping must be compact and lock-free to look up.
Devon: Refcounting model question: who owns the token lifecycle? Caller or runtime? I think caller gets a handle and must call `release_token` when done. Otherwise leak. But that surfaces lots of caller churn.
Marta: Maybe hybrid: runtime holds a soft ref while token exists; caller can promote to strong ref via `pin(token)` which prevents eviction. Default is soft ref that allows eviction but preserves ability to resume.
Anya: That aligns with our offload story. Soft refs = cheap, allow eviction; pin = barrier. We'll document semantics clearly.
Kevin: Telemetry: we need counters for how often fast alloc returns staging token vs resident, average time to promote, and misprediction rate of policy hints. Add perf histograms.
Marta: Also need a migration plan: 1) RFC and API surface, 2) perf harness + microbench, 3) feature-flagged rollout on one Dedicated pool, 4) gather telemetry and adjust heuristics.
Devon: I'll write the refcount/pin semantics doc and a few unit tests for race cases (pin during async-migrate, release during compaction).
Anya: I'll open the RFC follow-up today with the proto API + compatibility shim + checklist. Can someone pair on the perf harness?
Kevin: I can take the perf harness pairing.
ops-bot: created issue #4321: "allocator-api-strata: RFC follow-up + migration plan" — assigned to Anya.
Marta: +1 on the plan. One more ask: add a regression test that simulates high eviction pressure to ensure fast path latency doesn't regress.
Anya: Good call. Will add to checklist. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
